subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should first-time `agents.list` configuration be allowed to change the default agent by list order, or should OpenClaw require an explicit default/prompt when implicit `main` would be displaced?
rationale: The viable fixes intentionally change documented routing semantics, warning behavior, or config-write UX, and automation should not choose that product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Gate config writes with explicit default
options.body: Keep the runtime parser compatible, but make CLI/UI/doctor flows prompt or fail when a first non-empty `agents.list` has no `default: true` and existing `main` state would be displaced.

options.title: Warn only
options.body: Preserve first-entry fallback everywhere and add a high-visibility warning plus docs/doctor guidance for users adding their first listed agent.

options.title: Auto-preserve main
options.body: Materialize `main` as the default when `main` state exists, protecting continuity but changing the meaning of first-entry-only configs.

recommendation.title: Gate config writes with explicit default
recommendation.body: Keep the runtime parser compatible, but make CLI/UI/doctor flows prompt or fail when a first non-empty `agents.list` has no `default: true` and existing `main` state would be displaced.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the multi-agent routing/default behavior and is the strongest history signal for the product/security decision.
